facts.raw_span: continuous chest pain for two hours
denied dyspnea, syncope, or prior similar episodes
no personal or family history of cardiovascular or thromboembolic disease
sinus rhythm with 2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3
right ventricular dilatation and an estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg
continuous chest pain for two hours
denied dyspnea, syncope, or prior similar episodes
no personal or family history of cardiovascular or thromboembolic disease
sinus rhythm with 2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3
right ventricular dilatation and an estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg

concepts.why: The patient presented with continuous chest pain and ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3, which are indicative of acute coronary syndrome.

The patient had ST-segment elevation and was taken to the catheterization laboratory, but coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries, which may indicate a myocardial infarction with spontaneous reperfusion.
The patient developed a new right bundle branch block and had right ventricular dilatation, which are indicative of right ventricular infarction.
The patient had hypoxia and pulmonary hypertension, which may be indicative of pulmonary embolism, although the primary presentation was chest pain and ST-segment elevation.
The patient had right ventricular dilatation and a new right bundle branch block, which may be indicative of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

rationales.F01: Chest pain is a common symptom of acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: ST-segment elevation is a hallmark of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: New right bundle branch block is consistent with right ventricular infarction.
rationales.F11: Normal coronary arteries without stenosis make acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction less likely.
rationales.F12: Right ventricular dilatation and elevated pulmonary arterial pressure are consistent with right ventricular infarction and pulmonary embolism.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with right ventricular dilatation, estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg, and new right bundle branch block supports Right Ventricular Infarction, despite the absence of coronary stenosis.
